title: The Traffic Light That Exploded
description:
The world's first traffic light exploded. London, 1868: outside Parliament, a railway engineer, John Peake Knight, borrowed an idea from trains: swinging signal arms by day, red and green gas lamps by night, worked by hand by a policeman. About a month later, gas leaked into the post and the lamp exploded, hurting the policeman. London scrapped it, and traffic lights didn't come back for about sixty years. But the red and green came straight from the railways.

Would you have stood next to it?

More true whys: https://www.youtube.com/@truewhys?sub_confirmation=1

Sources: ITV News London (2018); CIHT, "Traffic light anniversary reached in London"; PA / Express & Star (2018); MoneyWeek, "10 December 1868". Accounts differ on the exact date of the explosion and how badly the constable was hurt.
Animation, music and sound: TrueWhys (original). Fonts: Lilita One (Open Font License).
